entry.title: Incident with Pages and Actions
entry.summary: Sep 16, 22:08 UTC Resolved - On September 16, 2024, between 21:11 UTC and 22:20 UTC, Actions and Pages services were degraded. Customers who deploy Pages from a source branch experienced delayed runs. Approximately 1,100 runs were delayed long enough to get marked as abandoned. The runs that weren't abandoned completed successfully after we recovered from the incident. Actions jobs experienced average delays of 23 minutes, with some jobs experiencing delays as high as 45 minutes. During the course of the incident, 17% of runs were delayed by more than 5 minutes. At peak, as many as 80% of runs experienced delays exceeding 5 minutes. The root cause was a misconfiguration in the service that manages runner connections, which caused CPU throttling and led to a performance degradation in that service. We mitigated the incident by diverting runner connections away from the misconfigured nodes. We are working to improve our internal monitoring and alerting to reduce our time to detection and mitigation of issues like this one in the future. Sep 16, 21:55 UTC Update - Actions is experiencing degraded performance. We are continuing to investigate. Sep 16, 21:53 UTC Update - The team is investigating issues with some Actions jobs being queued for a long time and a percentage of jobs failing. A mitigation has been applied and jobs are starting to recover. Sep 16, 21:52 UTC Update - Pages is operating normally. Sep 16, 21:37 UTC Update - Actions is experiencing degraded availability. We are continuing to investigate. Sep 16, 21:31 UTC Investigating - We are investigating reports of degraded performance for Actions and Pages

entry.title: Processing delays to some Issues, Pull Requests and Webhooks
entry.summary:
Sep 13, 07:13 UTC Resolved - On Sep 13, 2024, between 05:03 UTC and 07:13 UTC, the Webhooks and Actions services were degraded resulting in some customers experiencing delayed processing of Webhooks and Actions Runs. 0.5% of Webhook deliveries were delayed more than 2 minutes during the incident. 15% of Actions Runs started between 05:03 and 05:24 UTC saw run start delays or failures. At 05:24 UTC, we implemented a mitigation to shift traffic to healthy infrastructure and new Actions Runs resumed normal operations. During the rest of the incident window, Actions runs started before 05:24 UTC continued to see delays publishing logs or job results. No Actions runs or Webhook deliveries were lost, only delayed. We mitigated the incident by immediately shifting traffic to a healthy cluster while investigating. The incident was caused by an erroneous configuration change on our eventing platform. A permanent fix was deployed at 06:22 UTC after which services began to recover and burn down their backed up queues, with full recovery by 07:13 UTC. We are working to reduce our time to detection and develop test automation to prevent issues like this one in the future.
Sep 13, 06:49 UTC Update - We are seeing improvements in telemetry and are monitoring the delivery of delayed Webhooks and Actions job statuses. Sep 13, 06:23 UTC Update - We've applied a mitigation to fix the issues being experienced in some cases with delays to webhook deliveries, and the delayed reporting of the outcome of some running Actions jobs. We are monitoring for full recovery. Sep 13, 05:59 UTC Update - Actions is experiencing degraded performance. We are continuing to investigate. entry.title: Payment processing with Cartes Bancaires
entry.summary:
New!
Action required
You may have recently been informed by Stripe that an update was required to comply with EU regulations for co-badged cards.
New regulations specify that, in the EEA, businesses handling co-branded cards are required to offer customers the option to choose their preferred network during checkout. Rest assured, we have made the necessary updates to ensure that your guest payments are compliant with this regulation. As such, when a cardholder is using a cobadged Cartes Bancaires to pay on a Smily payment page, they are now required to select their preferred network.
Note: if you use Stripe, there are two requirements to accept Cartes Bancaires payments: Firstly you need to enable this option in your Payment Gateway settings on Smily.
Secondly, you may need update your payment methods in your Stripe settings to be able to accept Cartes Bancaires payments.
For more information, check out our dedicated manual article.

Should you need any assistance, we’re always here to help.

entry.title: Disruption with some GitHub services
entry.summary: Sep 5, 17:24 UTC Resolved - Between August 27, 2024, 15:52 UTC and September 5, 2024, 17:26 UTC the GitHub Connect service was degraded. entry.title: Incident: A small number of users experiencing lagging behavior when using mentions on Android
entry.summary:
Issue summary: From August 27, 2024, at around 8:17 PM PDT until August 28, 2024, around 1:39 PM PDT, some Android users experienced performance issues while trying to use mentions.
We rolled back a feature flag related to the message composer on Android. This change unexpectedly introduced an error in backend logic when users attempted a mention, causing the UI to become overwhelmed and unresponsive. We identified the cause and re-enabled the feature, gradually rolling it out to users and resolving the issue for those affected.
We also determined that the app crash issue mentioned in our updates was unrelated to the performance issues. You can review our summary of that incident here: https://slack-status.com/2024-08/459426ecb123c558. We apologize for any confusion.
